titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Solomon’s Petition and Charge to Jeroboam (ch. 69)
part: ch. 69 — Solomon’s Petition and Charge to Jeroboam
about: Solomon asks the angel when the saviour will come and is told: in forty-three generations, from his own seed, after Israel has crucified him. Grieved for his people, he laments in words close to the Wisdom of Solomon: the king and the poor share one grave, breath is smoke, and the name is forgotten in three generations. He then charges his son Jeroboam to do good and shun other gods, orders the words written down, and has Zadok anoint Jeroboam king while he lives.

sentences.t: ፷፱ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ስእለተ ፡ ሰሎሞን ።
sentences.l: 69. Concerning request-of Solomon
sentences.i: Chapter 69: Concerning the Petition of Solomon
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ ‘concerning’; ስእለተ is the construct (here also accusative) of ስእለት ‘request, petition’, a noun from ሰአለ ‘ask’, governing ሰሎሞን: ‘the request-of Solomon’, that is, the request Solomon makes in the unit that follows, not one made to him.

sentences.t: ወተመይጠ ፡ ወአንቃዕደወ ፡ ኀበ ፡ መልአክ ፡ ወሰፍሐ ፡ ክልኤሆን ፡ እደዊሁ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ቀርበኑ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ለመድኅን ፡ ዘትቤ ፡ ወሚመ ፡ ርሑቅኑ ፡ አውሥአ ፡ መልአክ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ በ፵ወ፫ ፡ ትውልድ ፡ እምዘመድከ ፡ ወእምዘርእከ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ ወያድኅነክሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-turned and-he-looked-up toward the-angel and-he-spread both-of-them his-hands and-he-said: O-Lord, is-it-near the-coming-of the-saviour which you-said, or is-it-far? The-angel answered and-said-to-him: In-43 generation from-your-kin and-from-your-seed he-will-come and-will-save-you;
sentences.i: He turned, looked up toward the angel, spread out both his hands, and said, “O Lord, is the coming of the saviour you spoke of near, or is it far?” The angel answered him and said, “In forty-three generations he will come from your kin and from your seed, and will save you;
sentences.n: Solomon speaks to the angel who has spoken since ch. 67 and addresses him as እግዚኦ, the vocative of እግዚእ. Verbs in ወ- + 3ms perfect: ወተመይጠ (tä-stem ‘turn’), ወአንቃዕደወ (‘lift the eyes’, a causative-reflexive stem, ‘look up’; I take this sense (?)), ወሰፍሐ ‘spread out’; ክልኤሆን is ‘both’ with the feminine suffix because እደው ‘hands’ is taken as feminine. ቀርበኑ and ርሑቅኑ are perfect and adjective with the question-enclitic -ኑ (‘is it near? is it far?’), ወሚመ ‘or’; ዘትቤ is ዘ- ‘which’ + 2ms ትቤ, the prefix form of the defective ይቤ used as a perfect. ምጽአቱ ‘his coming’ (ምጽአት + -ሁ). The number ፵ወ፫ with በ- reads ‘in forty-three’ (spoken አርብዓ ወሠለስቱ, arbəʿa wä-śälästu), followed by the singular ትውልድ ‘generation’, as is normal after a numeral; ‘forty-three’ is the text’s count (Matthew 1:17 counts three groups of fourteen). እምዘመድከ = እም- ‘from’ + ዘመድ ‘kin’ + -ከ; ወያድኅነክሙ is the 3ms of the causative አድኀነ ‘save’ + -ክሙ ‘you (pl.)’, the plural here because the line of Solomon is meant. The reply is cut at ፤ because it continues. The saviour’s coming and the crucifixion are prophesied here in plain terms.

sentences.t: ወእስራኤልሰ ፡ ይጸልኡ ፡ መድኀኒቶሙ ፡ ወይቀንኡ ፡ ላዕሌሁ ፡ በዘገብረ ፡ ተኣምረ ፡ ወመንክረ ፡ በቅድሜሆሙ ፡ ወይሰቅልዎ ፡ ወይቀትልዎ ፡ ወይትነሣእ ፡ ወያድኅነክሙ ፤
sentences.l: but-Israel-indeed they-will-hate their-saviour and-they-will-be-jealous against-him because-of-what he-did wonder and-marvel before-them, and-they-will-crucify-him and-they-will-kill-him and-he-will-rise and-will-save-you;
sentences.i: but Israel will hate their saviour and will be jealous against him because of the wonders and marvels he did before them; they will crucify him and kill him, and he will rise and save you;
sentences.n: ወእስራኤልሰ = ወ- + እስራኤል + the contrastive -ሰ ‘as for Israel’. ይጸልኡ ‘they hate’ (ጸለአ) and ይቀንኡ ‘they are zealous, jealous’ (ቀንአ) are 3mp imperfects; ላዕሌሁ ‘against him’ (ላዕለ + -ሁ). በዘገብረ = በ- ‘because of’ + ዘ- + ገብረ ‘(that) which he did’, with ተኣምረ ወመንክረ ‘wonder and marvel’ as accusative objects in apposition. The three verbs ይሰቅልዎ ‘they will crucify him’, ይቀትልዎ ‘they will kill him’, ይትነሣእ ‘he will rise’ (tä-stem of ንሥአ), with -ዎ ‘him’ added to the first two; the resurrection has no object because it is intransitive. The unit ends on the same promise of salvation, ‘and he will save you’, as the angel’s first clause.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ መሓሪ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ለነሳሕያን ፡ ወኄር ፡ ለኅሩያኒሁ ፤
sentences.l: for merciful he to-the-penitent and-kind to-his-chosen-ones;
sentences.i: for he is merciful to the penitent and kind to his chosen ones;
sentences.n: መሓሪ is the active participle of ምሕረ ‘be merciful’; ውእቱ ‘he’ is the copula. ለነሳሕያን = ለ- + ነሳሕያን, plural of ነሳሒ ‘one who repents’ (from ነሰሐ ‘repent’). ወኄር ‘and good, kind’; ለኅሩያኒሁ = ለ- + ኅሩያን ‘chosen ones’ + -ሁ ‘his’. A short unit for an explanatory clause (እስመ ‘for’) that answers the harshness of the previous one: the angel moves from Israel’s crime to God’s pity.

sentences.t: ወናሁ ፡ ነገርኩክሙ ፡ ጥዩቀ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢየኀድገክሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሲኦል ፡ ለዘመዲ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ እለ ፡ ተጸውረት ፡ ባሕርይ ፡ ኀቤክሙ ፡ ወዘንተ ፡ ብሂሎ ፡ መልአከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይቤሎ ፡ ሰላም ፡ ለከ ።
sentences.l: And-behold I-told-you certainly that not-he-will-leave-you in Sheol, for-kin (?) of-Israel who was-carried the-pearl with-you; and-this having-said the-angel-of God he-said-to-him: Peace to-you.
sentences.i: And now I have told you for certain that he will not leave you in Sheol, you the kin (?) of Israel, among whom the pearl was carried.” And having said this, the angel of God said to him, “Peace to you.”
sentences.n: ወናሁ ‘and behold’; ነገርኩክሙ ‘I told you (pl.)’ (1cs perfect + -ክሙ); ጥዩቀ ‘certainly’ (accusative of ጥዩቅ used as an adverb). ከመ ኢየኀድገክሙ ‘that he will not leave you’: negative ኢ- + 3ms subjunctive ይኀድግ of ኀደገ (the ይ- becomes የ- after ኢ-; a 1cs form would begin with አ-) + -ክሙ; the subject is the saviour of the preceding speech (?); ሲኦል ‘Sheol’, the place of the dead the saviour will empty. ለዘመዲ እስራኤል is doubtful (?): ለ- + ዘመድ ‘kin’ with a final -ዲ I cannot identify (an enclitic like -ሂ ‘also’, or a corrupt spelling), and the ለ- may mark the object or the persons addressed; I read it as an address, ‘you, kin of Israel’ (?). እለ ተጸውረት ባሕርይ ኀቤክሙ is a plural relative with a 3fs verb (‘who’ governing ‘the pearl was carried’); ተጸውረት is the passive of ጾረ ‘carry’, ባሕርይ ‘the pearl’ is the image of the saviour’s line (ch. 68), and ኀቤክሙ ‘with/among you (pl.)’. ብሂሎ is the gerund of the defective verb ‘say’ (‘having said’), ወዘንተ ‘and this’ (accusative); መልአከ is the construct of መልአክ before እግዚኣብሔር. The angel’s closing ሰላም ለከ is a greeting at leave-taking.

sentences.t: ወአውሥአ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ብቊዐኒ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ አሐተ ፡ እስአለከ ፡ ወኢትትሀየየኒ ፡ ገዓርየ ።
sentences.l: And-answered Solomon and-said-to-him: Help-me (?) my-lord, one I-ask-you, and-do-not-turn-away-from-me (?) my-cry.
sentences.i: Solomon answered and said to him, “Help me (?), my lord; I ask you one thing, and do not turn away from me (?) at my cry.”
sentences.n: Hard words (?). ብቊዐኒ = ብቊዕ, the 2ms imperative of በቊዐ ‘be of use, help’ (the verb of ኢይበቊዕ ‘it does not avail’ below) + -ኒ ‘me’: ‘help me’, a plea; the exact sense of the plea I hold as uncertain (?). አሐተ is ‘one (thing)’ in the accusative (feminine), ‘I ask you one thing’ (እስአለከ = 1cs of ሰአለ + -ከ). ወኢትትሀየየኒ is 2ms jussive with ኢ-: the verb ተሀየየ is read ‘turn away from’ (?), as in ch. 60 (ተሀየየኒ ‘turned from me’); ገዓርየ ‘my cry, my wailing’ (+ -የ ‘my’) stands in apposition to -ኒ or gives the occasion, ‘at my cry’ (?).

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ በል ፡ ተሰአለኒ ፡ ወአነ ፡ ኣየድዐከ ፡ ዘሰማዕኩ ፡ ወዘርኢኩ ።
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-him: Say, ask-me, and-I I-will-tell-you what I-heard and-what I-saw.
sentences.i: He said to him, “Speak: ask me, and I will tell you what I have heard and what I have seen.”
sentences.n: በል ‘say, speak’ (imperative of ብህለ), ተሰአለኒ ‘ask me’ (2ms imperative of the tä-stem of ሰአለ + -ኒ). ኣየድዐከ is spelled with ኣ- (the 1st person ‘I’ prefix ordinarily written አ-); it is 1cs imperfect of አይድዐ ‘make known’ + -ከ ‘to you’, ‘I shall tell you’. ዘሰማዕኩ ወዘርኢኩ = ዘ- ‘what’ + 1cs perfects of ሰምዐ ‘hear’ and ርእየ ‘see’: the angel offers what he himself has heard and seen.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ባሕቱ ፡ አሐዝን ፡ በእንተ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ሕዝቡ ፡ እለ ፡ ኀረየ ፡ እምኵሉ ፡ በትረ ፡ ርስቱ ፡ ቀዳሜ ፡ በኵሩ ፤
sentences.l: And-said-to-him Solomon: But I-grieve for Israel, his-people who he-chose from-all, rod-of his-inheritance, first-of his-firstborn;
sentences.i: Solomon said to him, “But I grieve for Israel, his people, whom he chose out of all, the rod of his inheritance, the first of his firstborn;
sentences.n: አሐዝን ‘I grieve’ (1cs of ሐዘነ). እለ ኀረየ is a plural relative with a singular verb (‘who he chose’), a looseness the text allows: ‘the people who, he chose’. እምኵሉ ‘from all’ = እም- + ኵሉ. በትረ ርስቱ ‘rod-of his inheritance’ is a construct chain (በትር, ርስት + -ሁ ‘his’); it recalls Psalm 74:2 (‘the tribe/rod of your inheritance’) and Jeremiah 10:16. ቀዳሜ በኵሩ is ‘first-of his firstborn’, a pleonasm that stresses Israel’s rank, after Exodus 4:22, ‘Israel is my firstborn son’.

sentences.t: ትቤለኒ ፡ ይጠፍኡ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ መጽአ ፡ መድኅን ።
sentences.l: You-said-to-me: They-will-perish after has-come the-saviour.
sentences.i: You told me that they will perish after the saviour has come.”
sentences.n: ትቤለኒ ‘you said to me’: ትቤ is the prefix form of ይቤ in the 2ms, with -ለኒ ‘to me’. ይጠፍኡ ‘they will perish’ (3mp imperfect of ጠፍአ). እምድኅረ ‘after’ + a perfect: ‘after the saviour came’. The whole unit is Solomon’s reproach.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ አውሥኦ ፡ መልአከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ እወ ፡ ነገርኩከ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሰቅልዎ ፡ ለመድኅን ፡ ወሶበ ፡ ከዐዉ ፡ ደሞ ፡ በዲበ ፡ ዕፀ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ይከውኑ ፡ ዝርዋነ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዓለም ።
sentences.l: And-again answered-him the-angel-of God and-said-to-him: Yes, I-told-you that they-will-crucify the-saviour, and-when they-poured-out his-blood upon tree-of cross they-will-be scattered ones into all world.
sentences.i: Again the angel of God answered him and said, “Yes, I told you that they will crucify the saviour; and when they have poured out his blood upon the wood of the cross, they will be scattered over the whole world.”
sentences.n: ወካዕበ ‘and again’; አውሥኦ = አውሥአ ‘answered’ + -ኦ ‘him’ (the person answered is the object); መልአከ is the construct before እግዚኣብሔር. እወ ‘yes’; ነገርኩከ ‘I told you’. ለመድኅን is the object marked by ለ-, doubling the -ዎ ‘him’ on ይሰቅልዎ. ወሶበ ከዐዉ: ሶበ ‘when’ + 3mp perfect of ከዐወ ‘pour out’ (the dispersion follows the shedding of blood); ደሞ is ደም ‘blood’ + the 3ms suffix -ኦ ‘his’, as in ገጾ ‘his face’. ዕፀ መስቀል is ‘tree-of cross’, a construct chain, ‘the wood of the cross’. ይከውኑ ዝርዋነ is ‘they will be scattered ones’, with ዝርዋነ (accusative of ዝርው ‘scattered’) as the predicate; the dispersion of Israel is the answer to Solomon’s grief.

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ እበክዮሙ ፡ ለሕዝብየ ፤
sentences.l: And-said Solomon: I-will-weep for-them, for-my-people;
sentences.i: Solomon said, “I will weep for them, for my people;
sentences.n: እበክዮሙ = አ- (1cs) + በክየ ‘weep’ + -ሙ ‘for them’ (the subjunctive, ‘let me weep’, would be spelled the same); ለሕዝብየ = ለ- + ሕዝብ + -የ ‘my’, a ለ- doubling the suffix -ሙ. Solomon’s lament begins here and runs through the unit that ends ‘there is no one who remembers our name’, and echoes Ecclesiastes and, further on, the Wisdom of Solomon.

sentences.t: አሌሎሙ ፡ ለሕዝብየ ፡ እለ ፡ ዘልፈ ፡ ያምዕዑ ፡ ፈጣሪሆሙ ፡ እምቀዳሚ ፡ ወእስከ ፡ ደኃሪ ፡ አነ ፡ ወእለ ፡ እምቅድሜየ ፡ ወኢይደሉ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይምሐሩነ ፡ በእንተ ፡ እከየ ፡ ምግባሪነ ፡ እስመ ፡ ትውልድ ፡ ዘአልብነ ፡ አሚነ ፤
sentences.l: Woe-to-them, to-my-people who always they-provoke their-creator, from-first and-until last, I and-those who before-me, and-not it-is-fitting that they-have-mercy-on-us (?) because-of evil-of our-deeds, for generation which not-we-have faith;
sentences.i: woe to them, my people, who have always provoked their Creator to anger, from the first to the last, I and those before me; and it is not right that mercy be shown us (?) because of the evil of our deeds, for we are a generation that has no faith;
sentences.n: አሌሎሙ is አሌ ‘woe’ + ለ- + -ሙ ‘to them’ (a cry of lament, like Latin vae). ያምዕዑ is 3mp imperfect of the causative አምዐወ ‘provoke to wrath’ with ፈጣሪሆሙ ‘their creator’ as object (+ -ሆሙ). እምቀዳሚ ወእስከ ደኃሪ ‘from first to last’. ወእለ እምቅድሜየ = ‘and those who (were) before me’ (እም- + ቅድሜ- + -የ). ወኢይደሉ is ኢ- + 3ms of ደለወ ‘be fitting’; ይምሐሩነ ‘they (should) have mercy on us’ is a 3mp subjunctive of ምሕረ (with ሐ, ‘be merciful’, not ምሀረ ‘teach’), whose subject is unexpressed (God, in honorific plural, or ‘those who judge’) (?). በእንተ እከየ ምግባሪነ = ‘because of the evil-of our deeds’ (a construct, with the suffix -ነ on the last noun). ዘአልብነ አሚነ = ዘ- ‘which’ + አልብነ ‘we have not’ (አልቦ + 1cp) + አሚነ ‘faith’ (accusative).

sentences.t: አሌሎሙ ፡ እለ ፡ ይክዕዉ ፡ ደመ ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ ወእለ ፡ ይጠቅሉ ፡ ጻድቀ ፡ ወይትካፈሉ ፡ በርበራቲሁ ፡ ወኢየአምኑ ፡ በቃሉ ፡ ወኢየሐውሩ ፡ በትእዛዙ ፤
sentences.l: Woe-to-them who they-pour-out blood innocent and-those who they-seize (?) righteous and-they-divide his-spoils and-not they-believe in-his-word and-not they-walk in-his-commandment;
sentences.i: woe to those who shed innocent blood, and who seize (?) the righteous man and share out his spoils, and who do not believe in his word nor walk in his commandment;
sentences.n: ይክዕዉ ‘they pour out’ (3mp imperfect of ከዐወ, as in the previous unit) with ደመ ንጹሐ ‘innocent blood’ (ንጹሐ accusative of ንጹሕ). ይጠቅሉ is unclear (?): I take it as a verb of seizing or binding with ጻድቀ ‘the righteous one’ as object (the saviour, though the plural may be general); the verb is not known to me (ጠቀለ ‘wrap, bind’ may be meant (?)). ይትካፈሉ በርበራቲሁ ‘they share out his spoils’ (tä-stem of ከፈለ ‘divide’; በርበራት ‘plunder’ + -ሁ ‘his’), recalling the soldiers dividing the garments, Matthew 27:35. ወኢየአምኑ ‘and they do not believe’ (አምነ) and ወኢየሐውሩ ‘they do not walk’ (ሖረ), with በቃሉ ‘by/in his word’ and በትእዛዙ ‘in his commandment’ (the -ሁ ‘his’ of the suffixed noun contracts to -ሉ, -ዙ).

sentences.t: ጽኑሕ ፡ ደይኖሙ ፡ ወንቡር ፡ ጌጋዮሙ ፡ ዐቢይ ፡ መቅሠፍቶሙ ፡ ወጽኑሕ ፡ ኀጢአቶሙ ፡ ወኢይሰሪ ፡ ሎሙ ፡ ወያዜክሩ ፡ ኀጢአተ ፡ አበዊሆሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ ምግባሮሙ ፡ ኀጢአት ፡ ወይትሀጐሉ ፡ በዘመከሩ ፡ ለሊሆሙ ፤
sentences.l: Firm their-judgment and-abiding their-guilt, great their-punishment and-firm their-sin, and-not it-is-forgiven to-them, and-they-bring-to-remembrance sin-of their-fathers, for their-deeds sin, and-they-perish by-what they-planned themselves;
sentences.i: their judgment is firm and their guilt abiding, their punishment is great and their sin heavy, and it is not forgiven them; they call to mind the sin of their fathers, for their deeds are sin, and they perish by what they themselves plotted;
sentences.n: The clauses are verbless adjective + noun-with-suffix (‘firm their-judgment’), each ‘X is Y’: ጽኑሕ ‘firm’, ንቡር ‘abiding, standing’, ዐቢይ ‘great’. The nouns are ደይን ‘judgment’, ጌጋይ ‘guilt, fault’, መቅሠፍት ‘scourge, punishment’ and ኀጢአት ‘sin’, each + -ሙ ‘their’. ኢይሰሪ is 3ms of ሰርየ ‘be forgiven’ with ኢ-, ሎሙ ‘to them’. ያዜክሩ is the 3mp causative (አዜከረ) of ዜከረ ‘remember, mention’ (the verb of ይዜክር in the last unit of the lament), ‘they bring to mind’ (?); the subject is unclear, and the unit may mean ‘they recall [as a defence] their fathers’ sin’, or ‘[their sin] reminds [God of] their fathers’ sin’ (?). ኀጢአተ is the construct before አበዊሆሙ ‘their fathers’. ይትሀጐሉ ‘they perish’ (tä-stem of ሀጐለ); በዘመከሩ = በ- + ዘ- + መከረ ‘counsel, plan’ + ለሊሆሙ ‘they themselves’; the thought is that the wicked fall into their own pit (Psalm 7:15 is the idea).

sentences.t: ወባሕቱሰ ፡ አሌላ ፡ ለነፍስየ ፡ እስመ ፡ ከበርኩ ፡ አኀስር ፡ በሞትየ ፡ ወተጠበብኩ ፡ በዲበ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወእከውን ፡ ሐመደ ።
sentences.l: But-indeed, woe-to-her, to-my-soul, for I-have-become-great (?) I-lose by-my-death, and-I-was-wise upon earth, and-I-shall-be dust.
sentences.i: But woe to my soul: for I have grown great (?), and I lose by my death; I became wise upon the earth, and I shall be dust.
sentences.n: ወባሕቱሰ ‘but indeed’ (ወ- + ባሕቱ + the contrastive -ሰ), then the turn from Israel to himself: አሌላ is አሌ + ለ- + -ኣ ‘her’, the feminine of አሌሎሙ above (ነፍስ ‘soul’ is feminine): ‘woe to her, to my soul’, the same doubling as አሌሎሙ ለሕዝብየ; ለነፍስየ ‘to my soul’ (ለ- + ነፍስ + -የ). ከበርኩ is 1cs perfect of ከብረ ‘be heavy, great, honoured’, and አኀስር 1cs imperfect of ኀሰረ ‘suffer loss’ (?), በሞትየ ‘through/by my death’: so the sense is probably ‘I have become great, yet I am the loser through dying’ (?). ተጠበብኩ is 1cs perfect of ተጠበበ ‘be wise, skilled’; ሐመደ ‘ashes, dust’ in the accusative, as predicate of ወእከውን ‘and I shall be’ (Genesis 3:19, Ecclesiastes 3:20).

sentences.t: ምንት ፡ ኅይስናሁ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ኢገብረ ፡ ሠናየ ፡ በዲበ ፡ ምድር ፡ ምስለ ፡ ነዳያን ፤
sentences.l: What his-excellence (?), the-king’s, if not he-did good upon earth with poor ones;
sentences.i: What is the worth (?) of a king if he has done no good on earth with the poor?
sentences.n: ምንት ‘what?’; ኅይስናሁ = ኅይስና ‘goodness, excellence’ (?) (so glossed in ch. 27 and ch. 33–34) + -ሁ ‘his’, which anticipates the owner that ለንጉሥ then names (‘his excellence, the king’s’, as in መስቀሎ ለመድኅን); the sense is ‘what is the king’s worth’ (?). ለንጉሥ = ለ- + ንጉሥ ‘for the king’; ለእመ ‘if’ (ለእመ + ኢ-); ገብረ ሠናየ ‘did good’ (ሠናየ accusative of ሠናይ); ምስለ ነዳያን ‘with the poor ones’. The unit is cut at ፤ because the next clause is balanced against it.

sentences.t: አሐቲ ፡ ድቀቶሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መቃብር ፡ ወአሐቲ ፡ ፍኖቶሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መዓምቅት ፤
sentences.l: One their-falling into grave and-one their-way into depths;
sentences.i: one is their fall into the grave, and one their way into the depths;
sentences.n: አሐቲ, the feminine of ‘one’, with ድቀት ‘fall’ and ፍኖት ‘way’ (feminine nouns in -ት + -ሙ ‘their’, hence -ቶሙ in both). The two halves are parallel: king and poor man end in the same grave. መዓምቅት ‘depths’ (plural of ዐምቅ ‘deep place’ (?)); the picture is Ecclesiastes 9:2–3, ‘one fate for all’.

sentences.t: ምንት ፡ በቊዔትነ ፡ ለሰብእ ፡ እስመ ፡ በከ ፡ ተፈጠርነ ፡ ወእምድኅረ ፡ ንስቲት ፡ ንከውን ፡ ከመዘ ፡ ኢተፈጠርነ ፤
sentences.l: What our-benefit for-man, for by-you (?) we-were-created and-after little we-shall-be like-one-who not-we-were-created;
sentences.i: What is our benefit, as men, since we were created by you (?), and after a little while we shall be as though we had never been created;
sentences.n: በቊዔትነ = በ- ‘in’ + ቊዔት ‘benefit’ + -ነ ‘our’; ለሰብእ ‘for man’. በከ ተፈጠርነ is uncertain (?): በ- + -ከ ‘by/in you’ would suddenly address God (or the angel) in the lament, which is abrupt but grammatical (‘we were created by you’); the word may instead be corrupt (?). I translate it as written and flag it. ተፈጠርነ is the 1cp passive perfect of ፈጠረ ‘create’. ወእምድኅረ ንስቲት ‘and after a little’ (ንስቲት ‘little’ as noun, fem.); ንከውን ‘we shall be’; ከመዘ = ከመ + ዘ- ‘like one who’, the two written together. The thought, and what follows it, comes from Wisdom of Solomon 2:2–5 (‘we were born by chance, and afterwards we shall be as though we had never been’), which the chapter is putting in Solomon’s mouth.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ጢስ ፡ እስትንፋስነ ፡ ለእመ ፡ አርመመት ፡ ሕቀ ፡ ተኀልፍ ፡ ነፍስነ ፡ ወቃለ ፡ ቀለምጽጽልብነዘይትሐወስ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ኅሊናነ ፡ እምከመ ፡ ኀለፈት ፡ ንከውን ፡ ሐመደ ፡ ወያስቆርሩነ ፡ ፍቁራኒነ ፡ ወማኅፈርነ ፤
sentences.l: for smoke our-breath, if it-grows-still a-little it-passes our-soul, and-word-of ቀለምጽጽልብነዘይትሐወስ in our-mind; after it-has-passed we-shall-be dust and-they-grieve-us (?) our-beloved-ones and-our-shame (?);
sentences.i: for our breath is smoke, and if it falls still for a little our soul passes away; and the word of [ቀለምጽጽልብነዘይትሐወስ, run together; unclear] in our mind. When it has passed we shall be dust, and our loved ones and our shame (?) will grieve us (?);
sentences.n: The source has a run-together string, ቀለምጽጽልብነዘይትሐወስ, which does not divide cleanly. Before it stands ወቃለ ‘and the word-of’ (ቃል in the construct), so the string would be the thing the word belongs to; I do not translate it (?); ልብነ ‘our heart’ and ዘይትሐወስ ‘which is stirred, moves’ (tä-stem of ሐወሰ) are present in it, and the whole may correspond to Wisdom 2:2, ‘speech is a spark struck from the beating of our heart’ (?), but I cannot make the reading certain. The rest: ጢስ ‘smoke’ (Wisdom 2:2: ‘the breath in our nostrils is smoke’), እስትንፋስነ ‘our breath’, ለእመ ‘if’, አርመመት ‘it falls silent’ (3fs perfect of አርመመ), ሕቀ ‘a little’, ተኀልፍ ‘it passes’ (3fs); the soul ነፍስነ is feminine. እምከመ ኀለፈት ‘after (when) it has passed’; ንከውን ሐመደ ‘we shall be dust’. ያስቆርሩነ is a 3mp causative with -ነ ‘us’, probably ‘they make us sorrowful, they grieve us’ (?), the verb not identified. ፍቁራኒነ is ‘our beloved ones’ (ፍቁራን + -ነ ‘our’, with the plural’s joining vowel, as in ኅሩያኒሁ above), and ማኅፈርነ ‘our shame’ or ‘our place of shame’ (?).

sentences.t: ወአእምሮ ፡ ኅሊናነ ፡ ዘመልዕልተ ፡ ርእስነ ፡ እምከመ ፡ ተክዕወት ፡ ነፍስነ ፡ ንከውን ፡ ዕፄ ፡ ወጺአተ ፤
sentences.l: and-knowledge-of our-mind which above our-head, after is-poured-out our-soul, we-shall-be ዕፄ ወጺአተ (crux);
sentences.i: and the knowledge of our mind, which is above our head, when our soul has been poured out, we shall be ዕፄ ወጺአተ (unclear; see the note);
sentences.n: Crux (?): ዕፄ ወጺአተ, as in ch. 27 (there ዕፄ ወጺአት, left unread) and left as it stands. ዕፄ elsewhere is ‘emperor, king’, which does not fit here, and ወጺአተ may be ወ- + ጺአተ, perhaps for ጽአት ‘going out, departure’ (verbal noun of ወጽአ), which ch. 27 could not read (?); ‘we shall be [a] going-out’ is as far as I can go (?), and the whole may be an error for a clause meaning ‘we shall be as a passing breath’ (?). Apart from the crux: ወአእምሮ ‘and knowledge’ (verbal noun of አእመረ), ኅሊናነ ‘our mind’ (+ -ነ), ዘመልዕልተ ርእስነ ‘which (is) above our head’ (መልዕልተ ‘above’), ተክዕወት ‘was poured out’ (3fs passive of ከዐወ, as in the crucifixion speech above; the soul as a liquid, cf. Psalm 22:14).

sentences.t: ወሙቀተ ፡ ሥጋነ ፡ እምከመ ፡ ኀለፈት ፡ ከመ ፡ ወኢምንትኒ ፡ ንከውን ፡ ወከመ ፡ ሳሕወ ፡ ደመና ፡ ነኀልፍ ።
sentences.l: and-the-warmth-of our-flesh, after it-has-passed, like and-nothing-at-all we-shall-be, and-like the-dispersal (?) of-cloud we-pass.
sentences.i: and the warmth of our flesh, when it has passed, we shall be as nothing at all, and we pass away like the dispersal (?) of a cloud.
sentences.n: ወሙቀተ ሥጋነ ‘and the warmth-of our flesh’ (ሙቀት, a construct and accusative, + ሥጋ ‘flesh’ + -ነ ‘our’). The sentence is hanging, with ሙቀተ as an accusative of respect: ‘as for the warmth of our flesh’. ወኢምንትኒ ‘nothing at all’ (ወ- + ኢምንት ‘nothing’ + the enclitic -ኒ); ከመ ‘like’, the ወ- after it being redundant for the sense (‘like, and nothing at all’). ሳሕወ I cannot place (?): ‘dispersal, dissolving’ would fit the cloud (Wisdom 2:4, ‘our life will pass like the traces of a cloud and be scattered like a mist’), and ሳሕወ may be an accusative of ሳሐው, from a root ሰሐወ ‘dissolve, disperse’ (?). ነኀልፍ ‘we pass’ (1cp imperfect of ኀለፈ).

sentences.t: ምንተኬ ፡ አብዝኆ ፡ ነቢብኒ ፡ ኢይበቊዕ ፡ ወሥነ ፡ ላሕይኒ ፡ ይትሀጐል ፡ ወጽንዐ ፡ ነገሥትኒ ፡ ይጠፍእ ፡ ወኀይለ ፡ መኳንንትኒ ፡ ይትሀጐል ፡ ወኢይትረከብ ፤
sentences.l: What-then? Having-multiplied speaking-even, not it-avails; and-the-beauty-of the-fair-one too it-perishes, and-the-might-of kings too it-vanishes, and-the-strength-of princes too it-perishes and-not it-is-found;
sentences.i: What then? Even speaking at length does not help; the beauty of the fair one perishes too, the might of kings vanishes too, and the strength of princes perishes too and is not found;
sentences.n: ምንተኬ ‘what then?’ (ምንት + -ኬ). አብዝኆ ነቢብኒ: the infinitive ነቢብ ‘speaking’ (+ -ኒ ‘even, too’) with the gerund አብዝኆ (of አብዝኀ ‘make many’: ‘having multiplied’); I take it as ‘even speaking much’. ኢይበቊዕ ‘it does not avail’. ወሥነ ላሕይኒ = ሥን ‘beauty’ (accusative/construct) + ላሕይ ‘fair, beautiful’ + -ኒ ‘too’; ወጽንዐ ነገሥትኒ ‘the might-of kings too’ (ጽንዕ, construct; ነገሥት plural of ንጉሥ); ወኀይለ መኳንንትኒ ‘the strength-of princes too’ (መኳንንት). The verbs are 3ms imperfects of ‘perish’ (ይጠፍእ, ይትሀጐል) and ‘be found’ (ይትረከብ, tä-stem of ረከበ). The refrain -ኒ ‘too’ ends each of the three subjects.

sentences.t: ወኵልነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ጽላሎት ፡ ነኀልፍ ፡ ወእምድኅረ ፡ ኀለፍነ ፡ በሞት ፡ ይትረሳዕ ፡ ስምነ ፡ ወኢይትረከብ ፡ አሠርነ ፤
sentences.l: And-all-of-us like shadow we-pass, and-after we-have-passed in-death is-forgotten our-name and-not is-found our-trace;
sentences.i: and all of us pass like a shadow, and after we have passed away in death our name is forgotten and our trace is not found;
sentences.n: ወኵልነ ‘and all of us’ (ኵሉ + -ነ ‘our’). ጽላሎት ‘shadow’ (Wisdom 2:5, ‘our time is the passing of a shadow’; also Psalm 144:4). ኀለፍነ ‘we passed’ (1cp perfect); ይትረሳዕ ‘is forgotten’ (tä-stem of ረሰዐ); አሠርነ ‘our trace, footprint’ (አሠር + -ነ). The two passives close the thought in the same way: name and trace both vanish.

sentences.t: እምድኅረ ፡ ፫ ፡ ትውልደ ፡ ደቂቅነ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይዜክር ፡ ስምነ ።
sentences.l: After 3 generation-of our-sons not-is who he-remembers our-name.
sentences.i: After three generations of our sons, there is no one who remembers our name.”
sentences.n: ፫ is read as spoken ሠለስቱ (śälästu) ‘three’; ትውልደ is the construct, in the accusative, of ትውልድ ‘generation’, ‘generations-of our-sons’ (ደቂቅ + -ነ). አልቦ ዘይዜክር ‘there is none who remembers’ (አልቦ ‘there is not’, ዘ- ‘who’ + 3ms imperfect of ዜከረ ‘remember’). The unit ends Solomon’s lament; he now turns to his son.

sentences.t: ወሶቤሃ ፡ አንጸረ ፡ ገጾ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዮርብዓም ፡ ወልዱ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ ተዐገሳ ፡ ለእኪት ፡ ወግበራ ፡ ለሠናይት ፡ ከመ ፡ ትርከብ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ መዋዕለ ፡ በዲበ ፡ ምድር ፤
sentences.l: And-then he-directed his-face toward Jeroboam his-son and-said-to-him: My-son, endure evil and-do good, that you-find many days upon earth;
sentences.i: Then he turned his face toward Jeroboam his son and said to him, “My son, endure what is evil and do what is good, that you may live long on the earth;
sentences.n: ወሶቤሃ ‘and then’; አንጸረ ገጾ ‘he turned his face’ (አንጸረ ‘look toward’, as in earlier parts; with ገጽ ‘face’ it is ‘turn, direct the face’; ገጽ ‘face’ + -ኦ ‘his’ in the accusative). The name is spelled ዮርብዓም here but ኢዮርብዓም in the last unit and in earlier parts: the same man, Solomon’s son in this text (the biblical Jeroboam of 1 Kings 11–12 is not Solomon’s son; Bezold’s text gives the name where Rehoboam would be expected, as in ch. 68). ተዐገሳ is the imperative of ተዐገሠ ‘bear, be patient’ + -ኣ ‘it (f.)’; ለእኪት ‘the evil (thing)’ and ለሠናይት ‘the good (thing)’ are the objects, marked by ለ-, both fem. nouns. ግበራ = the imperative of ገብረ + -ኣ ‘do it’. ትርከብ ‘you find, obtain’ (2ms subjunctive of ረከበ), ብዙኀ መዋዕለ ‘many days’, a phrase from the Law (Deuteronomy 5:33, ‘that you may live long’).

sentences.t: ወኢትስግድ ፡ ለአማልክት ፡ ባዕድ ፡ ወኢታምልኮሙ ፡ አላ ፡ ባሕቱ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ፍራህ ፡ ወአክብሮ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትማእ ፡ ፀረከ ፡ ወጸላእተከ ፡ ወበሰማያትኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትረስ ፡ ማኅደረ ፡ አበዊከ ፡ ወትረስ ፡ ሕይወተ ፡ ዘለዓለም ።
sentences.l: and-not-bow to-gods other and-not-worship-them, but rather God fear and-honour-him, that you-defeat (?) your-enemy and-your-foe, and-in-heavens-too that you-inherit dwelling-of your-fathers and-inherit life of-eternity.
sentences.i: do not bow down to other gods, nor worship them, but fear God and honour him, that you may overcome your enemy and your foe, and in the heavens too inherit your fathers’ dwelling, and inherit eternal life.”
sentences.n: ወኢትስግድ is the 2ms jussive of ሰገደ ‘bow down’ with ኢ-; ለአማልክት ባዕድ ‘to gods other’ (the plural አማልክት, with the singular adjective ባዕድ ‘strange’, the Geʿez idiom for ‘foreign gods’; Exodus 20:3, Deuteronomy 5:7). ወኢታምልኮሙ is 2ms jussive of አምለከ ‘treat as God, worship’ + -ሙ ‘them’. አላ ባሕቱ ‘but rather’; ፍራህ ‘fear!’ (imperative of ፈርሀ) and ወአክብሮ ‘and honour him!’ (imperative of አከበረ + -ኦ). ትማእ ‘you overcome’ is 2ms subjunctive of a verb I read as ‘conquer’, perhaps መውአ in a contracted spelling (?), ፀረከ ወጸላእተከ ‘your enemy and your foe’ (+ -ከ). ወበሰማያትኒ ‘and in the heavens too’ (ሰማያት, plural, + -ኒ). ትረስ (twice) is the 2ms subjunctive of ወረሰ ‘inherit’ (which gives ይረስ; ረሰየ ‘make, set’ would give ትረሲ), ማኅደረ አበዊከ ‘the dwelling-of your fathers’ (the construct; the promise is of a place for the dead patriarchs), ሕይወተ ዘለዓለም ‘life of eternity’. The same verb governs both objects, as with ርስት ‘inheritance’ above.

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ ጸሐፉ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መጽሐፈ ፡ ጡማር ፡ ወአንብራ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቀማጥር ።
sentences.l: And-he-said: Write for-me in book-of scroll (?) and-place-it in chest (?).
sentences.i: Then he said, “Write for me in a book, a scroll (?), and place it in the chest (?).”
sentences.n: ጸሐፉ is the 2mp imperative of ጸሐፈ ‘write’ (the form is the same as the 3mp perfect), addressed to scribes who are not named; ሊተ ‘for me’; መጽሐፈ ጡማር is a construct, ‘book-of scroll’ (ጡማር is the Greek tomarion ‘scroll’ in a Geʿez form, I believe (?)), and ወአንብራ ‘and put it’ is a 2ms imperative of አንበረ with -ኣ ‘it’, an odd shift from plural to singular. ቀማጥር I do not know (?); ‘chest, case for books’ is what the sense wants (?).

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ ለሳዶቅ ፡ ካህን ፡ ቅብኦ ፡ ወአንግ ፡ ሦ ፡ ለወልድየ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said-to Zadok priest: Anoint-him and-make-him-king my-son;
sentences.i: He said to Zadok the priest, “Anoint him and make him king, my son,
sentences.n: ቅብኦ is the 2ms imperative of ቀብአ ‘anoint’ + -ኦ ‘him’. አንግ ፡ ሦ is split by a wordspace in the source, which is an error (?); it is one word, አንግሦ, the imperative of አንገሠ ‘make king’ + -ኦ ‘him’ (the ሠ + ኦ coalescing to ሦ). ለወልድየ ‘my son’ in apposition, with ለ- marking the object, doubling the suffix. ሳዶቅ Zadok, the priest who anointed Solomon (1 Kings 1:39).

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ አንገሠኒ ፡ አቡየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ሕያው ፡ አነሂ ፡ ኣነግሦ ፡ ለወልድየ ፡ ኢዮርብዓም ፡ ወይኩን ፡ ዘርኡ ፡ መድኀኒትየ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ወለአበውየ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፡ በከመ ፡ ነገረኒ ፡ መልአከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: as he-made-king-me my-father David my-lord while living, I-also I-will-make-him-king my-son Jeroboam, and-may-be his-seed my-salvation to-me and-to-my-fathers until for-ever, as he-told-me the-angel-of God ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: as my father David, my lord, made me king while he lived, I too will make my son Jeroboam king; and may his seed be my salvation, mine and my fathers’, for ever, as the angel of God told me.”
sentences.n: በከመ ‘as’ + አንገሠኒ ‘he made me king’ (3ms perfect + -ኒ); the 1 Kings 1 account of David making Solomon king while he lived (1 Kings 1:32–48). እንዘ ሕያው ‘while living’ (እንዘ + the adjective). አነሂ ‘I too’ (+ -ሂ). ኣነግሦ is spelled with ኣ- (cf. ኣየድዐከ above): it is 1cs imperfect of አንገሠ + -ኦ ‘him’, ‘I shall make him king’. ኢዮርብዓም here, against ዮርብዓም in the charge above. እንዘ ሕያው አነሂ could instead be read ‘while I too am alive’, with ኣነግሦ (?); I take እንዘ ሕያው with David, as in 1 Kings 1. ወይኩን ዘርኡ መድኀኒትየ ‘and may his seed be my salvation’ (jussive of ኮነ; ዘርእ ‘seed’ + -ኡ ‘his’; መድኀኒት ‘salvation’ + -የ ‘my’); the saviour is to come from the line of Jeroboam, according to the pearl-doctrine of ch. 68, and Solomon is acting on that promise. ለአበውየ ‘for my forefathers’ (አበው, plural of አብ), እስከ ለዓለም ‘until for ever’. መልአከ is the construct before እግዚኣብሔር. The final run ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ marks the end of the chapter and has no ። before it; it stays with the last unit.
